h: Turn a practical stop into a proper seaside day
p: The great thing about Ocean Plaza's position is that you're surrounded by Southport's seafront attractions. Pleasureland, the town's amusement park, is close by for rides and thrills, while the Marine Lake gives you a lovely loop for a walk, with the light sparkling off the water on bright days.

King's Gardens, beside the lake, have been beautifully restored and are a lovely spot for families, with lawns, paths and the model railway village, which young children adore. Bring a picnic on a sunny day and you can make a whole afternoon of it without spending much at all.

Southport's beach is vast and flat, and the tide goes out a very long way. It's great for a bracing walk or flying a kite, but keep an eye on the tide and stick to the areas close to the promenade with little ones.

If you've got a car and time to spare, the Sefton Coast heading south has some of the largest sand dune systems in England, with nature reserves at Ainsdale and the National Trust's pinewoods at Formby, where you may be lucky enough to spot red squirrels.
Back at Ocean Plaza, parking your car here can make life easier if you're planning to walk to the seafront and back, so look at the signs for current charges and any time limits.
